transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07, 10:00 AM UTC | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Redwood SRE); Lena Ortiz, Marcus Lee, Aisha Khan, Tom Bauer, Jing Wu (FinSecure)

Summary: Quick recap of last week's incident where FinSecure saw intermittent 5xx and timeouts during peak batch ingestion. We discussed root causes (rate limiter/edge proxy + KV cache hot keys), mitigation steps taken, and next steps for deeper telemetry and a short benchmark run.

Topics: incident timeline, request patterns, rate limits and retry behavior, KV cache warmup, dedicated vs hosted capacity, security/compliance questions, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We'll go about 45 minutes. Quick roll call - can you say hi?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here.
[00:09] Marcus Lee: Marcus from infra. We had the logs ready.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Aisha product, here.
[00:14] Tom Bauer: Tom security.
[00:16] Jing Wu: Jing engineer.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. From our side Diego and I and Priya and Samir. We want to focus this meeting on the P0 incident last Friday and the follow-ups, and then set a short benchmarking window.

[00:30] Diego Alvarez: Quick context: we saw a cluster of 502/503s tied to a spike in long tail requests. There were also client-side retries that exacerbated burst. Some of the 5xx traces show a KV cache miss pattern - hot keys causing backend fetch storms.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: Agree. We also observed the gateway returning 504s after 15s. Our retry logic currently does exponential backoff with at most 3 retries, but many requests are synchronous so the user sees error.
[01:02] Jing Wu: To add, the traffic pattern included an unusual prefix-heavy batch where sequences were long, so runtime memory pressure increased and we saw slow kernels.

[01:20] Diego Alvarez: Right. There's a couple of moving parts: the edge proxy rate limiter and our serving runtime's batching/compaction. During the spike, the edge cut over to 50QPS limit per connection and some client SDKs didn't respect the 429, they kept retrying immediately.
[01:40] Maya Chen: We also traced a subset of 5xx headers that show a mismatch between model variant selection and available GPU kernels - in plain terms, the runtime fell back to a slower path and latency shot up.

[02:05] Marcus Lee: Is this primarily a hosted capacity problem or something we'd still see on Dedicated?
[02:12] Diego Alvarez: Good question. The root causes are not purely capacity. On Dedicated you'd avoid noisy neighbor effects and you'd have pinned capacity, but misconfigured client retries and hot-keying would still be an issue unless you use prefix/KV caching and request shaping.
[02:31] Lena Ortiz: We were debating dedicated because of predictability, but worried about cost. Can you quantify the burst/overage cost if we stay hosted?
[02:39] Maya Chen: We'll send a modeled estimate for that. Short answer: if you hit sustained peak we recommend reserved Dedicated; for short bursts we have burst-capacity pricing. I'll follow up with numbers.

[03:00] Aisha Khan: On the security side, Tom has questions about logs and audit trails in the incident. Tom?
[03:06] Tom Bauer: Yeah we need immutable audit logs and KMS-wrapped request payload logs for the post-mortem; is that available in hosted? Also want to know rollover for logs and whether we can get a signed SOC2 artefact for the incident.
[03:20] Priya Rao: For hosted we provide structured audit logs and you can stream them to your S3 with KMS. We can produce an incident pack for SOC2 review; Diego/Samir will pull the relevant traces.
[03:30] Samir Patel: We'll bundle the kernel selection logs and runtime traces but note some of the client-side retry headers are missing - Marcus can you include those?
[03:38] Marcus Lee: Yes we will pull them from our proxy.

[03:50] Jing Wu: Back to technicals - Diego, you mentioned KV cache hot keys. Can you explain what we should do to avoid that?
[03:58] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Two steps: first, prefix-awareness in the client so you don't hammer the same prompt prefix (we saw lots of identical preambles). Second, enable our prefix-KV caching with a warmed pool; if you have long sequences, we recommend a cache warming pass during ingest. Also set sensible sticky routing for long-lived sessions.
[04:24] Lena Ortiz: Is cache warming automatic on Hosted?
[04:27] Diego Alvarez: We do automatic prefix caching for common prefixes but explicit warm-up is best for one-off large batches. On Dedicated you can control the eviction TTL.

[04:40] Marcus Lee: The 504s at the edge - are they coming from our proxy timing out or Redwood's frontend?
[04:46] Diego Alvarez: The 504s are from the gateway layer (the reverse proxy) when backend token generation exceeded the configured timeout. We recommend increasing the timeout to 30s for ingest pipelines with long sequences and tune client retry to jittered backoff. But there's a tradeoff with user-facing latencies.

[05:10] Aisha Khan: Regarding retries, we saw clients configured to do immediate retries on 5xx; that created thundering herd. Any recommended backoff pattern?
[05:18] Maya Chen: Exponential backoff with capped jitter, and honor 429/Retry-After. We can share an SDK patch that respects server-supplied Retry-After and adds full jitter.
[05:35] Jing Wu: Can Redwood upload a small instrumentation agent or sample headers so we can match traces?
[05:40] Diego Alvarez: We'll prepare a trace mapping doc and a small header sniffing script - Diego to share by Monday.

[05:55] Marcus Lee: For the model path fallback causing slow kernels, is that something likely to recur?
[06:02] Samir Patel: Kernel fallback happens when the runtime chooses quantized vs native kernels mismatched to sequence length and available CUDA/cuD kernels. We're improving heuristics; in the short term we can pin a model variant for your pilot to avoid fallback.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Pinning sounds good for the POC. How do rollouts work? If we pin, will we lose auto-updates?
[06:27] Diego Alvarez: You can pin a model version in the route config, and still get patch releases. We'll coordinate canary updates. For our recommendation: pin for the POC testing window, then open to gradual rollouts.

[06:45] Aisha Khan: On compliance: Tom, anything else?
[06:48] Tom Bauer: Also want to confirm RBAC for console access and whether audit logs include token-level cost attributions.
[06:55] Priya Rao: RBAC yes, SSO (SAML) works, and we can give token-level cost breakdowns in the console export.

[07:05] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap what we'll deliver: 1) Redwood to share filtered request logs, kernel logs, and trace mapping (Diego/Samir) 2) Customer to export retry headers and proxy traces (Marcus) 3) Short benchmark on 2026-05-12 to reproduce the peak with both hosted and dedicated simulation (Diego/Marcus) 4) Pricing for Dedicated/reserved + burst options (Maya) 5) Incident pack for SOC2 (Priya).

[07:40] Marcus Lee: Quick question: for benchmarking, can we get a temporary dedicated pool for one day?
[07:46] Maya Chen: We can offer a short-term reserved pool for testing at a reduced rate for the POC bench; I'll include pricing options in the follow-up.

[07:58] Jing Wu: Anything about client SDK versions? We saw some clients on older SDKs that didn't handle 429s properly.
[08:04] Diego Alvarez: We'll flag the minimum SDK and share a patch; recommend upgrading to 1.4.3 which includes better Retry-After honor.

[08:18] Tom Bauer: For the post-mortem, can you include a timeline with UTC stamps and a blameless summary? We'll need that for our audit.
[08:24] Priya Rao: Yes, we'll prepare a blameless incident timeline.

[08:35] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[08:38] Lena Ortiz: One last note - we will test with a replay of the failing payloads and let you know if we can reproduce locally.

[08:45] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send the notes and action items after this call. Thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: there are a few transcription artefacts - some proper nouns were mis-transcribed (kernel names, internal route ids), and speaker labels may be off in one block where the audio overlapped.

End of transcript.

Recap and next steps (short):
- Diego/Samir: share kernel logs + trace mapping + SDK patch (due 2026-05-10)
- Marcus: export proxy retry headers and failing payloads (due 2026-05-09)
- Maya: pricing for dedicated/reserved + burst and short-term test pool (due 2026-05-11)
